state: "Two days afterward he came on board to see me. I was mate, then, on the Duchess, a whacking big one-hundred-and fifty-ton schooner, a blackbirder. And let me tell you that blackbirders were blackbirders in those days. There weren't any government protection for US, either. It was rough work, give and take, if we were finished, and nothing said, and we ran niggers from every south sea island they didn't kick us off from. Well, Saxtorph came on board, John Saxtorph was the name he gave. He was a sandy little man, hair sandy, complexion sandy, and eyes sandy, too. Nothing striking about him. His soul was as neutral as his color scheme. He said he was strapped and wanted to ship on board. Would go cabin boy, cook, supercargo, or common sailor. Didn't know anything about any of the billets, but said that he was willing to learn. I didn't want him, but his shooting had so impressed me that I took him as common sailor, wages three pounds per month. "He was willing to learn all right, I'll say that much. But he was constitutionally unable to learn anything. He could no more box the compass than I could mix drinks like Roberts here. And as for steering, he gave me my first gray hairs. I never dared risk him at the wheel when we were running in a big sea, while full-and-by and close-and-by were insoluble mysteries. Couldn't ever tell the difference between a sheet and a tackle, simply couldn't. The fore-throat-jig and the jib-jig were all one to him. Tell him to slack off the mainsheet, and before you know it, he'd drop the peak. He fell overboard three times, and he couldn't swim. But he was always cheerful, never seasick, and he was the most willing man I ever knew. He was an uncommunicative soul. Never talked about himself. His history, so far as we were concerned, began the day he signed on the DUCHESS. Where he learned to shoot, the stars alone can tell. He was a Yankee--that much we knew from the twang in his speech. And that was all we ever did know.

state: What does /pol/ think of skinheads? Skinheads may not have always been Nazis, but they sure as shit weren't ethnically tolerant. For those unaware, skinhead subculture started in Britain with the working class Hard Mod subculture. Lots of skinheads enjoyed Rock music, and then came the wave of Ska-loving Jamaican and West Indies immigrants. The immigrants brought Ska music with them which caught on hard with the skinheads, reaching a fever pitch in what many nostalgic skinheads call the Spirit of '69. Although predominantly white, the original skinheads were racially integrated with more than a fair showing of blacks in the group. Then came Punk Rock. Garry Bushell played roughly as influential a role with marketing Punk Rock to skinheads through his magazine The Sounds as Malcolm McLaren had with The Sex Pistols. White skinheads started identifying with Punk subculture in greater numbers. Soul, Ska and Reggae would soon be blended with Punk Rock to form a style called 2 Tone Ska. As this was all happening, Indians and Pakistanis became a much stronger presence in UK. Despite their racial integration, xenophobia was prevalent among even black skinheads. Violence against South Asians, known as Paki bashing, became common. Add some Punk Rock nihilism with the decimation of the working class under Neoconservatism's growing influence in two of the major Anglo powers and, presto, you've got the perfect storm. state: I left the Marines confused and lost. I traveled from place to place, picking up random laborer jobs. In a hick ass town in the Kentucky coal strip, an Italian family gave me a chance and taught me to be a brick-layer. I was an armorer in the Corps. I should have listened to my cousin and at least picked a liveable trade, but now I had one. I really wasn't making shit, but the cost of living was low. I'm still batshit insane, and a lot of what I went through still fucks with me, but my life was finally good, is good. As my life turned around, and the positivity began to shine through, one of their daughters fell for me. My wedding present was a house, a rent house, and a future business. On the downside, I have to have these really elaborate, drawn out Italian family dinners every night with my in-laws. As a third generation American, whose family is Bavarian Catholic, it is liveable, but my own family wonders why I have no time for their gatherings. My advise is to go out and live your life. Take chances and meet people. I wasn't looking for the love of my life when I found mine. I was just looking to live and keep from crawling full-time into a bottle.

state: The point of all this is that simply writing people off as sheeple, or worthless degenerates only partially hits the mark. Yes, the interconnectedness of everything allows what would normally be minor incidents or perversions to blossom, but it's the explosion of the force of opinion that is almost a greater danger. A kid in school who wants to be a communist is one thing. many years ago, that would be all. Isolated, with at best a few friends and supporters, it would most likely be dismissed as a phase and pass in time. However, now they can reach out to hundreds of thousands of others, and suddenly gain a sense of community and support that can turn a phase into a lifestyle choice. Toxic elements that would normally have the impact of a bad head cold are quickly turning into social plagues. We didn't used to be able to pick only the people we liked to interact with. We had to deal with whoever the hell it was who was around. By being forced to deal with people who we did not like, disagreed with, and who in turn didn't like and disagreed with us, we were also forced to develop a thicker skin. To make one's way through life, you had to accept that people with disagree with you. That your worldview was just that, yours, and others would at best accept only portions of it. Now, one can reach to another and wrap themselves in a blanket of constant support and praise. Now, the voices of dissent and difference are not the norm, but the outliers to be dismissed. Should we all just go backward and give up on modern society? No, but the time is rapidly approaching where we either need to accept whatever new world is building, reject it entirely and try to turn back the clock, or try to actually balance progress with humanity. there isn't one simple answer to this, it will likely take many elements of many ideologies to even start to fix, but trying to reach out and stabilize you own small circle is a start.

state: Meanwhile, he kept on trying to reach mainland Greece, from where his chances of progressing towards Western Europe would have been brighter. But he failed. Around June 2016, he was called for his interview. Shahid claimed that he was called for the interview a few days earlier than it was actually supposed to be. Underprepared and still naive to this whole thing, he failed the interview and his asylum application was consequently rejected in August. Life at a standstill Shahid Ali was housed at the infamous Moria Camp. His temporary stay was due to expire in October and since his asylum application had been rejected, an extension was not a possibility. Shahid’s dream of a life in Europe had come to standstill and the risks he took traveling through Iran with the help of smugglers meant nothing - or so it seemed. But there was a twist in his story. Help came from where he least expected it. Two local women from Moria Village helped Shahid and took him to the capital Athens in their car’s trunk. “I spent almost fifteen hours in the trunk of their car as we reached mainland Greece in a ferry. I did not get out of the trunk even when the car was on the ferry - there were strict controls and cameras everywhere.” Shahid added that when they reached their destination and he got out of the car, he was not able to walk for some time as his legs were stiff. But there was a sense of achievement as he had reached Athens, a buzzing city with opportunities. Next destination France Shahid Ali spent two weeks in a nearby village, seeking ways to migrate further towards Western Europe. Finally, he found someone. An African smuggler sold him a fake French identification card for 900 Euros. Shahid got himself a ticket to the French capital, Paris. The next part was a bit tricky, but somehow Shahid passed the immigration counter without much difficulty. “They asked me a few questions and then they let me go.”

state: With all this talk about the debate going on, I just wanted to take the time to make a couple points about what I believe "winning a debate" entails. Firstly, appearance is everything. A canidate could have all the best answers and be in the right, but if the delivery is too meek or convoluted, the other canidate can easily make it appear as though they provided the better answer. While I think that both canidates gave fairly weak answers tonight, Hillary certainly had the better demeanor and tone which gave the layman the impression that she won. Secondly, the entire point of a debate is to 1; renforce and clarify your positions and b, to win over potential supporters. Neither canidate really accomplished much in the first department, but to me it looked like Hillary more than likely won in the second category. Trump focused far too much on the people already voting for him instead of attempting to go after Clinton on issues that he could've made her look bad on and potentially swing voters. Trump (whether or not he actually was) appeared to be on the defense for the last 2/3rds of this debate, which gives the impression that he was losing. I was very underwhelmed by his performance tonight, but I feel as though the lack of ammunition he was throwing at Clinton may be because hes saving it for the last and most memorable debate. Before you say Lester was preventing Trump from speaking on those issues.Trump had no problem interrupting him to complete a thought. If he really wanted t,o he would have no issue interrupting to fire some heavy artillery at Clinton.
